title: The Protocol Can Be Drained Through Commitment Duplication
quote: it is possible to insert commitments without nullifying previous commitments. This is done by exploiting the construction of the input array to the Circom Verifiers. The duplicated commitments can later be withdrawn.
mechanism_one_line: Input array passed to the Circom verifiers can be built so new commitments are inserted without nullifying spent ones
unbound_value: nullifier/commitment dimensions of the verifier input array vs circuit
notes: Fix commit text: 'Validated Dimensions against Circom Data' (supports input-array dimension mismatch, P5).

title: Attackers Can Make Protocol Interactions Untraceable for Users
quote: since no integrity check of `encryptedOutputs` exists in the Solidity contracts or Circom circuits, a malicious relayer or a front-runner can arbitrarily change its value to alter the decrypted output to some random bytes.
mechanism_one_line: encryptedOutputs not bound by proof or contract; relayer/front-runner can alter it
consumer_effect: NewCommitment event logs tampered outputs; user cannot recover UTXOs (loss of funds)
notes: Front-running rule applied (stored value changes by third party). Auditor notes the attacker gains nothing; harm is to the user. Client fix: encrypted outputs added into callDataHash.

title: Deposited Funds Can Be Drained by a Compromised Owner
quote: the attacker can register a malicious contract that always returns `true` regardless of input.
mechanism_one_line: Owner of VerifierFacade can register a constant-true verifier
consumer_effect: Attacker claims others' commitments and transfers funds (stated)
notes: Listed under v1.1 verifier-soundness (constant-true verifier) but requires compromised privileged owner; flagged for human judgement. Mitigated only (role separation).

title: A Transaction May Not Distribute All Funds
quote: This creates an imbalance where the contract can keep more tokens than expected.
mechanism_one_line: _transact checks balanceDif >= amountChanges (inequality) against the proven amount
notes: Consumer enforces only a one-sided bound on a proof-fixed amount; attacker/beneficiary of the shortfall is not stated. Fix: inequality changed to equality.

title: Arithmetic Overflow in Circom Could Be Exploited to Drain Funds
quote: an attacker could forge some output commitments with a large token amount but whose sum results in a small number. They can then drain the funds in the protocol with the forged commitments.
mechanism_one_line: Swapper circuits add amounts modulo CIRCOM_P with no overflow check
notes: Auditor states the attack does not exist for the currently implemented Swapper circuits, only for future ones; hence BORDERLINE not KEEP. Missing range checks = P4.

title: Insufficient Validation of Access Token Existence
quote: an attacker can generate a ZK proof to prove an internal node of the Merkle tree is in the tree by setting `X` and `Y` to its left and right child.
mechanism_one_line: AccessTokenChecker accepts hash(X,Y) equal to an internal Merkle node
consumer_effect: Proof of access without an access token (impact stated as not currently exploitable)
notes: Auditor: may not currently impact the protocol because swapper circuits derive publicKey from shieldedPrivateKey.

title: Unconstrained `calldataHash` Could Lead to Attackers Re-Routing Funds
quote: This opens an opportunity for a malicious relayer or a front-runner to add external action calls and hooks that the user did not intend, as well as redirect funds to a different `externalAddress`.
mechanism_one_line: calldataHash is unconstrained in Circom; helper only checks hash against data, so a proof made for another hash passes
consumer_effect: Unintended external calls/hooks and redirected funds
notes: Front-running rule applied. Acknowledged, not fixed. Client says circom still yields unique proofs for unused public inputs (rebuttal noted, not weighed).

title: Potential Malleability Attacks on Nullifier Due to `Groth16`
quote: However, due to Malleability, generating another valid proof for the same inputs for the commitment is possible. This allows every commitment to be used twice.
mechanism_one_line: Groth16 proof malleability allows a second valid proof for the same inputs
consumer_effect: Commitment spendable twice (as stated by auditor)
notes: Decided on the auditor's text per section 2. Client rebuttal (acknowledged, no fix): a second proof with the same inputs would revert because nullifiers are recorded. AI doubt: with nullifiers as public inputs, proof malleability alone does not normally enable double spend; human label should check.

title: A Zero `signerAddress` Skips Both the Signature Check and the Replay Guard
quote: no nullifier is burned and no message is consumed, so the transaction leaves no trace that would stop it running again in the next block for the price of gas.
mechanism_one_line: Caller sets signerAddress=0 so verifyWallet skips signature check and usedMessages replay guard; minimal proof accepted
consumer_effect: Arbitrary ops executed from Emporium context, repeatable
verifier_present: PARTIAL (VerifierFacade.sol 200; generated Groth16 verifiers not in scope list)
notes: Low severity; Emporium is stateless so impact limited to stateless calls (see HIN-11 for asset theft). Client fix: usedMessages consumed on every path.

consumer_effect: Theft of assets stranded in Emporium or allowances granted to it

title: Missing Strict Validation of Critical x.509 Certificate Extensions
quote: The current implementation of Intel SGX PCK certificate validation logic does not explicitly verify critical X.509 extensions such as `Key Usage` (OID: `2.5.29.15`) and `Basic Constraints` (OID: `2.5.29.19`).
mechanism_one_line: Guest program's PCK certificate validation skips critical extensions
consumer_effect: Weak attestation could be proven; on-chain contract then registers enclave key (effect implied)

notes: Concerns what the on-chain contract is told (v1.2 circuit-only DROP excludes this case), so BORDERLINE. Auditor's mitigation (chain must be signed by a trusted root) is not weighed.
